# EAFIT promotes smart, sustainable and regenerative coffee farming in Antioquia

The project _"A coffee for sustainability and productivity"_ is an initiative led by EAFIT, in partnership with EIA University, the Technical University of Munich (TUM), Expocafé and the Salgar Coffee Growers Cooperative, in three locations in Antioquia: Caicedo, Concordia and the township of Altamira (Betulia).

The proposal seeks to strengthen 300 small coffee farmers through regenerative agricultural practices, community innovation and smart value chains, in order to face challenges such as climate change and adapt to international demands such as the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR).

- EAFIT Promotes Smart, Sustainable and Regenerative Coffee Farming in Antioquia

![Imagen EAFIT promotes smart, sustainable and regenerative coffee farming in Antioquia](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/31b700bd-6bf5-46b2-88ed-3c379c04e26c/web/Taller-Concordia.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=823&h=450&itok=eJVDBrP8)

The project, which began in July 2024, focuses on regenerating coffee-growing landscapes and promoting local economic development with a community-based approach. The image shows one of the workshops in the municipality of Concordia, in southwestern Antioquia.

Coffee farming in Antioquia faces urgent challenges stemming from climate change, pressure on ecosystems, and the new demands of international trade. In response to this situation, EAFIT University, through its Public Value Center, is leading the project " _A Coffee for Sustainability and Productivity_ ," an initiative in partnership with EIA University, the Technical University of Munich (TUM), Expocafé, and the Salgar Coffee Growers Cooperative.

“This proposal seeks to promote smart, sustainable and regenerative coffee value chains in Antioquia, increasing the competitiveness of MSMEs (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises), strengthening food security, boosting local economic development and preserving ecosystems through community collaboration,” says Harold Cardona-Trujillo, principal investigator of the project.

The initiative, which will last 24 months, is being implemented in three locations in Antioquia: the municipalities of Caicedo and Concordia, and the township of Altamira (Betulia). In its first phase, the project is working with a pioneering group of 45 coffee growers, and will then expand to 300 producers through three sequential meetings scheduled between April and June 2025.

One of the main challenges facing the coffee sector today is compliance with the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), which imposes specific requirements on agricultural exports. _"Coffee for Sustainability and Productivity"_ is positioned as a strategy to prepare communities for these new market conditions through sustainable adaptation processes.

Juan Carlos Muñoz Mora, a researcher at EAFIT's Center for Public Value and director of the project, explains that the methodology includes three main components: the co-design of a digital platform, the transformation of the value chain, and the connection with emerging markets. “What we are doing is applying a support model to rural communities so that, based on the use of evidence, literature, and existing knowledge, we can encourage the transition to more sustainable and inclusive production practices.”

This working model includes various activities that support communities in their transition from unsustainable practices to more environmentally responsible ones. In the first component, participatory methodologies are being used to develop the necessary tools for this transition, including a digital platform where producers, cooperatives, and rural advisors can interact with the intervention model.

The second component focuses on transforming the entire value chain, from producer to end consumer. The third component aims to directly connect this model with European importers. Through international partnerships, the goal is to establish trade relationships that recognize not only the quality of the coffee, but also the process behind its production.

#### First achievements and next steps

During its first few months, the project has already shown significant progress toward its objectives. The characterization of the participating communities has been completed, and a first functional version of the technological platform has been developed. In addition, an initial repository of good agroecological practices has been built, the first meeting using the World Café methodology was successfully held, and 15 educational videos have been finalized. The participation and commitment of the coffee growers have been key in this initial stage.

Among the expected results of the project are improved competitiveness for coffee-producing micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), strengthened food security, a boost to local economic development, preservation and restoration of ecosystems, and the establishment of regenerative value chains. These goals will be achieved through a combination of community actions, technological tools, and educational processes, aimed at consolidating a sustainable and resilient coffee farming model adapted to current challenges.

Con una base metodológica sólida y un enfoque participativo que ha favorecido la apropiación comunitaria, el proyecto continúa su avance conforme a lo planificado. La articulación entre estrategias presenciales, herramientas digitales y materiales audiovisuales ha creado un entorno de aprendizaje integral y adaptado a las realidades del territorio. Los meses que vienen serán decisivos para consolidar este modelo, ampliar su impacto y fortalecer la plataforma tecnológica como soporte clave para la sostenibilidad de esta apuesta por una caficultura con visión de futuro.

###### Virus contra bacterias, la propuesta para el sector porcino de PhageLife desde EAFIT

En una granja porcina, una infección bacteriana puede poner en riesgo la salud de los animales y la productividad del negocio. Además, el problema se vuelve más complejo cuando las bacterias dejan de responder a los antibióticos que antes permitían combatirlas. Para explorar otra vía, la empresa [PhageLife](https://phagelife.co/) desarrolla soluciones personalizadas con bacteriófagos, virus naturales capaces de eliminar bacterias específicas.
